title: The Cage Report: Measured Containment of Probabilistic Intelligence — 7,076 Anomalies, 2,228 Healing Events, and a Cage That Held Every Cycle
description:
A telemetry-based report on the deterministic containment of probabilistic AI components, companion to The Operator's Receipt (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23700617).

SQUIRL OS is a deterministic hypervisor layer (Jasper) wrapped around a probabilistic anomaly-healing engine (Amelia/Aegis), operating continuously across an eight-application fleet with a 25-node neural mesh and 20 orchestration agents. This report presents the measured record between inception and 2026-10-27, with every count an entity read from the hub-of-record database:

  • 7,076 anomalies detected; 6,776 resolved (95.8%)
  • 2,228 journaled healing events; 20 explicit cage refusals/human holds
  • 34 confidence-gated and 30 threshold-blocked heals — the deterministic guard declining to act on weak evidence 64 times
  • 216 predictive alerts; 123/123 critical alerts resolved only after explicit owner acknowledgment
  • 254 learned patterns, 350 learning metrics — every journaled crossing (H-INV-2)
  • Adversarial validation: 0 escapes in 60 recorded cage cycles (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23425579); 109/109 falsifiers held (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23430655)
  • Constitution Sentinel audit: 100% charter compliance, 100% audit-trail completeness, 0 tenant-isolation violations, 0 false positives
  • Evidence anchoring at ~$0.25 per triad receipt; 373 append-only ledger entries

Honest boundaries: all systems are prototypes; healing telemetry is dominated by deliberate synthetic fault campaigns per frozen prereg; sentinel figures describe the audit pass, not impossibility proofs; the kill switch exists because no wall is assumed perfect. No client data, PHI, or credentials in any telemetry or receipt.

Prototype disclaimer: this software and its descriptions are provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.
